_meta.purpose: Candidate deployment SITES per Applications-tab category (US + abroad), with the regulatory/utility filing trail for each. Complements opportunities.json: that file tracks buyer instruments; this file tracks named physical sites and their filings. Rows that correspond to a tracker row carry tracker_id and add site-level facts only.
_meta.method: Depth-first: deep rows were built by reading primary documents (docket searches via tools/adams_search.py + tools/ferc_elibrary.py, pages cached via tools/fetch_source.py and indexed in data/research/source_index.json with URL + access date + SHA-256). Scan rows come from click-through on the Applications tab's citations plus web search, each with at least one source. No row is written without a source.
_meta.filing_note: A filing entry is a document lodged with (or issued by) a regulator or utility forum: NRC ADAMS accessions, FERC eLibrary accessions, state PUC dockets, CNSC records. 'None located' gaps are honest absences after a docket-system search, not unchecked blanks.

negative_findings.finding: FERC eLibrary has zero filings with 'microreactor' in the description as of 2026-08-23 (tools/ferc_elibrary.py 'microreactor' --desc-only: totalHits=0). Microreactor deployments to date are behind-the-fence or distribution-level and do not touch FERC-jurisdictional dockets.

sources.label: FERC eLibrary search (API, description search)

negative_findings.finding: Malmstrom AFB's only FERC eLibrary filing ever is a 1994 Montana Power electric tariff for base service (ER94-801-000) — no modern interconnection filing exists for the ANPI eVinci project.

sources.label: FERC eLibrary — MT Power Co tariff w/ Malmstrom AFB (accession 19940107-0041)

_meta.category_absences: Categories where no named candidate microreactor site was located as of the capture date, beyond what opportunities.json already tracks: Mining (the IANC consortium is multi-site and unassigned; the tracker's counter-signal row stands), Agriculture & Food, Transportation (US — the one named port deployment is abroad, see the tracker's Thames Freeport row), and the hospital/prison/water bands of Civic Infrastructure. Honest absences, not unchecked blanks.
_meta.extra_categories_note: Deployment categories the Applications taxonomy (sectors.json) deliberately does not carry — that page maps civilian load types, while defense procurement is its own buyer frame (as in opportunities.json's tracks). Declared here with their allowed bands so a Sites UI can group these rows and so a row with an undeclared category fails the tests instead of being silently skipped.
_meta.janus_note: Added 2026-08-29: the five Army Janus installations announced 2026-08-26. They are recorded as scan depth, not deep — the announcement and trade coverage are the only public record. Unlike every other site here, a Janus reactor generates no NRC docket and no state utility filing, because the Army licenses it. Absence of a paper trail for these five is a feature of the contracting route, not a research gap.

sites.name: Penn State FRONTIER — eVinci-based research reactor
sites.summary: Penn State's FRONTIER Project told the NRC on 2025-02-17 it intends to file a Construction Permit application for a research reactor based on the eVinci design at University Park, at a thermal power of 15 MWt, under 10 CFR 50.21(c)/50.23 (AEA §104(c) nonprofit-educational pathway). The letter asks for a project number and a dedicated NRR project manager, and says a Regulatory Engagement Plan would be issued to the NRC later in 2025. The vendor's own pre-application docket (99902079) holds 244 documents from 2019 through 2026, including NRC safety evaluations of eVinci topical reports issued into mid-2026.

Vendor pre-application docket for eVinci (topical reports, safety evaluations, meeting records; 244 documents 2019–2026)

sites.utility_context: Campus behind-the-meter research facility; no state PUC or FERC filing expected for a §104(c) research reactor.

sites.name: Copper Valley Electric Association MMR (Valdez / Glennallen)
sites.band: Individual remote grids with sufficient year-round demand
sites.owner: Copper Valley Electric Association (member-owned cooperative, islanded grid)
sites.summary: The completed pre-feasibility study (USNC doc 027263, 2023-06-09) found an MMR 'a match for CVEA's needs': replacing the Valdez cogeneration unit, with CVEA ownership beating vendor ownership on economics, year-round heat sales pivotal, and IRA credits worth 30–50% of capital (energy-community + domestic-content bonuses, direct pay available). It evaluated a Mountain Site at ~Mile 3 Dayville Road, Valdez — a bedrock bench at the toe of Sugarloaf Mountain ~600 feet below the Trans-Alaska Pipeline, zoned Public Use / Heavy Industrial — as lowest tsunami risk and suitable for construction, plus a Glennallen site with no nearby heat off-taker. CVEA nonetheless tabled the project indefinitely on 2023-08-09. The paired state-policy artifact is Alaska SB 177 (signed 2022-05-24), which removed the legislative-designation requirement for reactor siting in AS 18.45.

filings.type: Pre-feasibility study, public release
Project tabled announcement
SB 177 — microreactor siting statute amendment (AS 18.45)

sites.utility_context: CVEA is the utility — an islanded cooperative serving ~3,800 members from Valdez to Glennallen, not interconnected to any other grid. No Regulatory Commission of Alaska docket for the project was located.

sites.name: Eielson AFB — DAF microreactor pilot site
sites.owner: U.S. Department of the Air Force (DLA Energy contracting)
sites.power: 5 MWe (2023 selection figure); DAF describes the class as 1–50 MW
sites.summary: The DAF's preferred site for the first commercial microreactor on a DoD installation. NOITA to Oklo announced 2025-06-11 (re-issued after the 2023 selection was rescinded); 30-year firm-fixed-price contract to follow NRC licensing; DAF and NRC are preparing the environmental analysis. Site logic: the base runs a 72-year-old coal-fired heat-and-power plant and buys electricity from Golden Valley Electric Association — the pilot is backup power and grid-independence for an Arctic F-35 base, taking electricity and heat under a long-term PPA.

sites.name: Global First Power MMR at Chalk River Laboratories
sites.owner: Global First Power (OPG + USNC joint venture)
sites.summary: The richest foreign filing trail in the microreactor class and the first SMR licence application in Canada (announced 2019-04-02): a licence to prepare site under NSCA s.24(2) plus a CNSC-led environmental assessment under CEAA 2012, for an MMR delivering up to 45 MWt of process heat via molten salt at Canada's national laboratory campus, ~200 km northwest of Ottawa. CNSC staff paused all EA and licence-review work in 2024; parent USNC filed Chapter 11 in October 2024. CNSC's project page now reads 'Current Status: Paused' and its review-status page is archived.

sites.name: Fort Bragg — Antares R1 three-pack (Janus)
sites.summary: Antares will own, build and operate a three-unit R1 deployment at Fort Bragg, home of the XVIII Airborne Corps, targeting 2028. Antares declined to disclose the contract value. Announced 2026-08-26 under the Army's Janus programme: up to $2.2bn across five installations and more than 20 reactors, running FY2027-FY2031 through fixed-price, milestone-based Other Transaction Authority agreements administered by the Defense Innovation Unit. The vendor owns, builds and operates the plant. These reactors are authorised by the Army Reactor Regulatory Office, not the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. After the Defense Innovation Unit funds construction and the first year of operation, the Army expects to move to a power purchase agreement. The reactors are tied into the installation grid and are not intended to carry the whole load. The Army expects most of the capital to be private.
sites.utility_context: Janus reactors sit behind the installation fence and are regulated by the Army, so no state utility commission docket or interconnection filing has been located for any of the five sites.
